label: Cave
_model: Wild kernel underground. The appetite belongs to the hole itself — it wants to be gone into, gone down, spoken to, and to keep whatever comes. Claimants are the cave's own names for itself, and the accommodation is what it did to whoever came in.

appetites.want: never to have a light brought into it
appetites.purpose: it would be dark all the way down
appetites.asks: "Why did you bring that in here?"

appeasement.move: put out a light of your own, deliberately, and stand in it

appetites.want: that everything which comes in should go further down
appetites.purpose: nothing would ever stop and go back up
appetites.asks: "Is that as far as you go?"

appeasement.move: go down one level further than you meant to

appetites.want: that everything said in it should be said back

appeasement.move: say something aloud into the dark and wait for it to come back

appetites.want: that nothing which comes in should ever leave
appetites.purpose: it would still have all of it
appetites.asks: "You're not taking that out, are you?"

appeasement.move: leave something of your own down here on purpose

accommodations.text: took {conscript} in and closed behind them
let {conscript}'s lights go out one by one
turned {conscript} around so gently they never noticed
grew over {conscript} where they sat down to rest
answered {conscript} in their own voices until they followed
kept {conscript} at the mouth, facing in, so the next lot would come

flame.label: the last flame that went out down here
flame.function: the only light that ever reached the bottom

plumb.label: the line that was let down and came back up
plumb.function: the only thing here that ever measured the depth

voice.label: the one word the cave says in somebody else's voice
voice.function: the only thing down here that was ever answered honestly

stone.label: the stone that grew around something and let it go
stone.function: the only thing the cave ever gave back

factions.name: the Kept
factions.essence: came in and never got out, and have stopped minding

factions.name: the miners
factions.essence: came down for the workings and cannot find the way up

factions.name: what the dark does when it is not watched
factions.essence: has never once been seen whole

factions.name: what came up from the sump
factions.essence: lives below the water and does not need to breathe

triggerGlossary.announced: came in at the mouth in daylight, with a light burning
triggerGlossary.seenTwice: passed the same formation twice, going different ways
triggerGlossary.loud: a raised voice underground, which the cave repeats
triggerGlossary.lingering: stayed still long enough for the cave to grow a little over you
triggerGlossary.disturbed: broke a formation, moved a cairn, or let a stone go down a pitch

skirmish.line: a Bat Swarm and 2 Giant Rats in the entrance chamber

foes.name: Bat Swarm
foes.note: douses open flames on a hit

skirmish.harmedBy: anything; area attacks and fire do best against the swarm
skirmish.avoid: shutter your lights and they lose interest entirely

foes.name: Ogre
foes.note: cannot follow into a crawl or a squeeze

fight.avoid: it cannot fit where you can — the crawl is the answer, and say so

battle.line: 1 Troll out of the sump and a Bat Swarm

foes.name: Troll
foes.note: REGENERATES 2 Grit a round unless the wound was burnt

foes.name: Bat Swarm
foes.note: douses open flames on a hit

battle.harmedBy: anything, but the Troll only stays down if fire touches it; the swarm douses open flames
battle.avoid: it will not leave the water; stay off the streamway and it stays in

nightmare.line: 1 Troll, 1 Ogre and 3 Ghouls of the Kept

foes.name: Ghoul
foes.note: free Called Shot to freeze on a hit

nightmare.avoid: do not run this without an appeasement route open and a way out at your back

dark.dangerLine: the cave has been dark for a very long time and it has not enjoyed the interruption

institution: a dark so complete that your eyes invent things in it
passages that have never had light in them at any point
a mouth where the daylight stops in a hard line
ritual: a candle set in a niche at every junction and lit going in
lights counted at the mouth and counted again coming out
a lamp left burning at the bottom for whoever is still down
demand: a niche with a candle in it, unlit, and the wick trimmed
a lamp guttering with the oil not yet gone
a hard line of daylight that stops exactly where you are standing
wound: candles in every niche, all of them burnt out together
a lamp smashed against the wall from the inside
a line of spent matches going one way down a passage
anchor: the last flame that went out down here
a lamp that has never needed filling
a candle that will light in any air

features: an unlit candle in a niche
a lamp guttering with oil left
spent matches in a line
a smashed lamp against a wall
burnt-out candles in every niche
daylight stopping in a hard line

decisions.cue: a niche with a candle in it, unlit, with the wick trimmed ready
decisions.cost: lighting it is a courtesy or an intrusion, depending

resolve.success: you light it and the cave lets you pass this junction unmolested, both ways
resolve.failure: you light it and something further in sees exactly where you are: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave the niche dark; the junction will not stay in the same place behind you

decisions.cue: a lamp guttering on the floor with oil still in the reservoir
decisions.cost: it is going out for a reason, not for want of fuel

resolve.success: you work out what is putting it out and can keep your own lights alive down here
resolve.failure: you refill it and it goes out anyway, and takes your lights with it
resolve.orElse: leave it; your own lights start to gutter within the Turn

decisions.cue: a line of spent matches going one way down a passage
decisions.cost: somebody was striking one at a time and losing them

resolve.success: you follow the matches and find where they ran out, and what they had reached
resolve.failure: you follow them the wrong way and come out somewhere you have already been
resolve.orElse: ignore them; you have no line to follow through the middle passages

decisions.cue: all the candles in every niche burnt out together, at the same length
decisions.cost: they went out at once, which takes doing

resolve.success: you find what put them out and can force it back for one scene with fire
resolve.failure: you relight the run and it happens again, to yours: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave them; the dark here is not ordinary and you will not know why

decisions.cue: a hard line of daylight stopping exactly where you stand
decisions.cost: crossing it is the last unambiguous decision you will make

resolve.success: you mark the line and can find your way back to it from anywhere
resolve.failure: you cross without marking it and the mouth is not where you left it
resolve.orElse: turn back at the line; the delve does not happen, and the cave keeps everything

decisions.cue: a lamp smashed against the wall from the inside
decisions.cost: somebody down here chose the dark

resolve.success: you find who broke it and why, and the reason is worth knowing
resolve.failure: you leave your own light where theirs was and something takes it too
resolve.orElse: leave the glass; you never learn what makes a person put their own light out

situations.doing: sitting in a niche with an unlit candle in its hands
situations.onArrival: it holds the candle out toward you without looking up
situations.because: the candle is lit going in and it never went in
situations.offer: light the candle for it and it will walk you to any junction here

situations.doing: striking matches one at a time in a passage
situations.onArrival: he asks how many you have left
situations.because: he has been going through them since his lamp failed
situations.offer: give him a light and he will show you the way the workings run

situations.doing: standing in a chamber where your lights do not reach the walls
situations.onArrival: your flames shorten as you come in and do not go out
situations.because: the cave has never had light this far in
situations.offer: put your lights out on purpose and it will let you through anything

situations.doing: carrying a lamp between them that is not burning
situations.onArrival: they stop and offer it to you, handle first
situations.because: the lamp goes to the bottom for whoever is still down
situations.offer: take the lamp down and everything here treats you as one of the party

situations.doing: burning in a niche in a passage nobody has entered
situations.onArrival: the flame leans toward the way you came in
situations.because: somebody lit it going in and never came back past it
situations.offer: take the candle and the cave will not put your lights out

situations.doing: showing as a hard line of daylight a long way behind you
situations.onArrival: the line is narrower than when you passed it
situations.because: the cave keeps what comes in and the mouth is how it does that
situations.offer: go back and touch the line and it stops narrowing

temptations.cue: a stub of the last flame
temptations.benefit: once, have light where light does not work
temptations.standingDrawback: the cave knows exactly where the flame is at all times

temptations.cue: a candle that lights in any air
temptations.benefit: your lights cannot be put out by the dark
temptations.standingDrawback: the dark attends to you personally instead

temptations.cue: a lamp that has never needed filling
temptations.benefit: light for as long as you want it
temptations.standingDrawback: it was somebody's and they are still using it

temptations.cue: a handful of dry matches
temptations.benefit: once, buy yourself one scene of light
temptations.standingDrawback: the count is finite and you will know when it runs low

temptations.cue: a mark cut at the daylight line
temptations.benefit: once, find your way back to the mouth
temptations.standingDrawback: whatever is between you and it also knows the way now

deep.dangerLine: the cave goes down further than anybody has been and it would like you to see

institution: a system that goes down in steps, each one further than the last
pitches rigged with somebody else's rope, still hanging
a survey that stops with the word CONTINUES
ritual: a stone dropped at every pitch head and counted down
the line let out and knotted at each ten fathoms
a cairn built at the deepest point reached
demand: a pitch head with a rope hanging down it and no knot at the bottom
a stone dropped that has not landed yet
a cairn half built at the lip of something
wound: a rope cut at the pitch head and the rest of it down there
cairns knocked flat all the way down
anchor: the line that was let down and came back up
a survey with a bottom marked on it

features: a rope hanging down a pitch
a half-built cairn at a lip
a survey ending mid-word
a cut rope end at a pitch head
knots at every ten fathoms
a stone that has not landed

decisions.cue: a pitch head with a rope hanging down it and no knot at the bottom
decisions.cost: the rope may not reach and there is no way to know from up here

resolve.success: you rig it properly off your own gear and get down and back with the rope still there
resolve.failure: you go down on it as found and it ends in air: you are down, and it is not coming back up
resolve.orElse: do not descend; the way on is through the sump instead, and the sump is worse

decisions.cue: a stone dropped at a pitch head that has not landed yet
decisions.cost: the count is still going

resolve.success: you count it out and know exactly what is below, and can plan for it
resolve.failure: you stop counting and go down on an assumption
resolve.orElse: throw nothing; you descend without knowing what is under you

decisions.cue: a cairn half built at the lip of something
decisions.cost: somebody was marking their deepest point and stopped

resolve.success: you finish the cairn and the cave accepts the mark — everything below it is passable
resolve.failure: you knock it and the cave stops acknowledging any depth you reach
resolve.orElse: leave the cairn; nothing down here will treat you as having got anywhere

decisions.cue: a survey ending mid-word with the word CONTINUES
decisions.cost: whoever wrote it went on and did not come back to finish

resolve.success: you read the survey and know the shape of everything below, including the way out
resolve.failure: you take the survey as complete and trust a passage that closes
resolve.orElse: leave it; you go down blind from here on

decisions.cue: a rope cut clean at the pitch head with the rest of it below
decisions.cost: somebody cut it from up here, on purpose

resolve.success: you find who was cut off and why, and what they became down there
resolve.failure: you splice on and go down after it, and it is cut again behind you
resolve.orElse: leave the rope; whoever is down there stays down there

decisions.cue: a line knotted at every ten fathoms, coiled and dry
decisions.cost: the knots say how far it has been

resolve.success: you use the line and can go down and come back up as often as you need
resolve.failure: you let the whole line out and the end goes on falling: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave the line; every descent from here is one-way

situations.doing: standing at a pitch head with a rope in its hands
situations.onArrival: it offers you the end and points down
situations.because: the pitch was never bottomed and it will not go alone
situations.offer: take the rope and it will hold it for you, indefinitely

situations.doing: dropping away into air at your feet with a rope hanging in it
situations.onArrival: a stone you did not throw is still falling
situations.because: it has never been bottomed and it wants to be
situations.offer: go down and the cave will let you back up, once

situations.doing: paying a line out over a lip and not stopping
situations.onArrival: they ask how deep you think it goes
situations.because: they have been letting it out since their lamps were full
situations.offer: tell them a depth and they will haul, and bring up what is on the end

situations.doing: building a cairn at a lip, stone by stone
situations.onArrival: it sets a stone and looks at you to approve it
situations.because: it was marking the deepest point reached and never reached further
situations.offer: add a stone and everything below this point lets you through

situations.doing: hanging pinned to a boulder with the last word unfinished
situations.onArrival: the ink of the last word is still wet
situations.because: whoever wrote it went on and the page waits
situations.offer: finish the word and the cave shows you what is beyond it

situations.doing: filling a chamber whose floor you cannot see
situations.onArrival: the air comes up warm and smells of somewhere else
situations.because: everything that comes in goes down and it is still waiting for you
situations.offer: go down willingly and it will not close behind you

temptations.cue: the line that came back up
temptations.benefit: once, know exactly what is below you
temptations.standingDrawback: what is below you knows the same about you

temptations.cue: a rope that reaches
temptations.benefit: once, get down and back up anything
temptations.standingDrawback: it reaches because something at the bottom is holding it

temptations.cue: the survey with a bottom marked
temptations.benefit: know the shape of the system below
temptations.standingDrawback: the marked bottom is not the bottom

temptations.cue: a stone off the deepest cairn
temptations.benefit: once, be treated as having got there
temptations.standingDrawback: the cave expects you to go further next time

temptations.cue: a knotted measuring line
temptations.benefit: measure any drop before you take it
temptations.standingDrawback: you will measure one you cannot avoid

echo.dangerLine: everything said down here comes back, and lately it has been coming back changed

institution: chambers shaped so that a word spoken at one end arrives whole at the other
a system that carries a voice further than a light
passages that answer in a different order than you spoke
ritual: a name called at every junction and waited for
the same phrase said at the entrance by everyone going in
a whistle used instead of shouting, three notes, always
demand: a chamber that has just stopped repeating something
a whistle answered from further in, correctly
your own voice arriving from a direction you have not gone
wound: a chamber that repeats a scream at the same interval
voices calling names of people who are not down here
an answer that comes before the call
anchor: the one word the cave says in somebody else's voice
a chamber that gives a true echo
a whistle that only carries to the living

features: a chamber still repeating something
a whistle answered from ahead
your own voice from the wrong direction
a name called at a junction
an answer arriving before the call
three notes with no whistler

decisions.cue: a chamber that has just stopped repeating something you did not say
decisions.cost: answering it starts a conversation

resolve.success: you answer carefully and the cave tells you, truthfully, where somebody is
resolve.failure: you answer freely and it has your voice now, and uses it: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: say nothing; whatever was calling calls somewhere else, to somebody else

decisions.cue: a whistle of three notes answered correctly from further in
decisions.cost: the answer means somebody living, or something that learned

resolve.success: you test it with a fourth note and know which, before you meet it
resolve.failure: you whistle back and go toward it, and it is the other one
resolve.orElse: stay silent; you never establish whether anybody else is down here

decisions.cue: your own voice arriving from a direction you have not gone
decisions.cost: the cave has kept it and is using it

resolve.success: you recognise it as yours and are not drawn — and you learn which passage it came from
resolve.failure: one of you follows it, briefly, and is separated
resolve.orElse: block your ears; you also cannot hear each other, for a Turn

decisions.cue: a name being called at a junction, over and over, for somebody not down here
decisions.cost: the caller does not know they are alone

resolve.success: you tell it the truth gently and it stops, and thanks you, and helps
resolve.failure: you answer to the name and it takes you for them: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: walk past; the calling follows you at exactly the same distance

decisions.cue: an answer that arrives before the call it answers
decisions.cost: the cave is ahead of you in the conversation

resolve.success: you work out what you are about to say and choose not to say it, which unnerves it
resolve.failure: you say the thing anyway and confirm that it knows you
resolve.orElse: ignore it; every route from here is chosen for you, quietly

decisions.cue: a chamber repeating a scream at exactly the same interval
decisions.cost: the interval is the useful part

resolve.success: you time it and use the gap to cross, or to be heard, exactly once
resolve.failure: you cross on the scream and everything down here turns toward the chamber
resolve.orElse: go the long way, costing a Turn, and hear it the whole way

situations.doing: calling a name at a junction with nobody there to own it
situations.onArrival: it stops when you arrive and starts again when you move
situations.because: somebody called and was never answered
situations.offer: answer to the name and every passage here will carry your voice truly

situations.doing: whistling three notes and waiting for the reply
situations.onArrival: it whistles again when it sees you, and waits
situations.because: the reply comes from further in and it will not go alone
situations.offer: whistle the reply and it will lead you to whatever has been answering

situations.doing: shouting measurements to somebody who is not writing them down
situations.onArrival: she asks you to repeat the last one back
situations.because: her partner stopped answering a long time ago
situations.offer: repeat it back and she will give you the survey she has made

situations.doing: filling a chamber with your own voice from a passage you have not entered
situations.onArrival: the voice says something you have not said yet
situations.because: the cave keeps voices and it has kept yours
situations.offer: let it finish and it will tell you one true thing in your own words

situations.doing: standing apart in a chamber and speaking in turn
situations.onArrival: they leave a gap in the exchange exactly the length of a sentence
situations.because: the third of them stopped speaking and they carried on
situations.offer: say anything into the gap and both will do whatever you ask

situations.doing: repeating a scream at the same interval in an empty chamber
situations.onArrival: the interval shortens slightly while you listen
situations.because: it happened here and the chamber will not let it go
situations.offer: name what happened and the chamber goes quiet, and stays quiet

temptations.cue: the word the cave says in another voice
temptations.benefit: once, be believed by anything that knew that person
temptations.standingDrawback: you say it in their voice and something of them comes with it

temptations.cue: a caver's whistle
temptations.benefit: once, be heard by everything living down here
temptations.standingDrawback: and by everything that is not

temptations.cue: a knack for the true-echo chamber
temptations.benefit: once, ask the cave a question and get an answer
temptations.standingDrawback: it asks one back, and expects it answered

temptations.cue: a name called and never answered
temptations.benefit: once, make something come to you
temptations.standingDrawback: it comes expecting the person whose name it is

temptations.cue: a stretch of passage that does not echo
temptations.benefit: once, move or speak without the cave hearing
temptations.standingDrawback: you cannot hear it coming either

keeping.dangerLine: the cave has kept everything that ever came in, and it is still adding

institution: formations grown over things that were not stone to begin with
a floor of bones with the newest ones on top
a system where nothing rots and nothing goes away
ritual: a thing left at the mouth by everyone going in
stone laid down a hair a year over whatever is under it
the dead left where they fall and grown into the floor
demand: a formation with a shape under it you can nearly make out
a shelf of offerings at the mouth with a gap in the row
a hand of stone reaching out of a wall, worn smooth
wound: formations broken off and carried out
a bone floor dug through in one place, recently
the mouth shelf swept clean and the offerings gone
anchor: the stone that grew around something and let it go
a formation with a whole thing visible inside it

features: a formation with a shape inside it
a gap in a row of offerings
a bone floor dug through
a stone hand worn smooth
broken flowstone carried out
a shelf swept clean

decisions.cue: a shelf of offerings at the mouth with a gap in the row
decisions.cost: filling the gap pays your way in

resolve.success: you leave something that genuinely costs you and the cave lets you back out
resolve.failure: you leave something worthless and it is noticed and remembered: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave the gap; the mouth will be smaller on the way out than the way in

decisions.cue: a formation with a shape under it you can nearly make out
decisions.cost: breaking it open frees what is inside, or ends it

resolve.success: you open it carefully and what is inside is grateful, and knows the way
resolve.failure: you break it and take the piece, and the cave starts growing over you
resolve.orElse: leave it grown over; whatever is in there stays in there, and it was watching

decisions.cue: a bone floor dug through in one place, recently
decisions.cost: somebody was looking for something in the older layers

resolve.success: you find what they dug for and get it before they come back
resolve.failure: you dig further and the floor gives out into what is under it
resolve.orElse: leave the hole; you never learn what is worth digging a bone floor for

decisions.cue: a hand of stone reaching out of a wall, worn smooth by touching
decisions.cost: people have been shaking it for a long time

resolve.success: you take the hand properly and the Kept accept you as one who came in politely
resolve.failure: you take it and it does not let go until you leave something behind
resolve.orElse: do not touch it; the Kept treat you as having walked past them

decisions.cue: broken flowstone stacked ready to be carried out
decisions.cost: somebody is taking the cave away in pieces

resolve.success: you find the carriers and can trade — they know every way out because they use them
resolve.failure: you carry a piece yourself and the cave will not let you out with it
resolve.orElse: leave the stack; the carriers stay hidden and unhelpful

decisions.cue: a stone that has grown around something and split, leaving it loose
decisions.cost: the cave gave one thing back, once

resolve.success: you understand what it took to make that happen and can do it again at the ending
resolve.failure: you pocket it and the cave takes the equivalent from you: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it; there is no precedent for the cave giving anything up

situations.doing: reaching out of a wall at the height of a handshake
situations.onArrival: the fingers are warm and worn smooth
situations.because: everyone who came in shook it and one of them did not let go
situations.offer: take the hand and the Kept will treat you as expected and welcome

situations.doing: sitting half grown into a flowstone curtain, still able to turn its head
situations.onArrival: it asks how long it has been
situations.because: it sat down to rest and the cave got on with it
situations.offer: give it a number and it will tell you where everything down here was left

situations.doing: stacking broken formations by the passage mouth
situations.onArrival: they ask whether you are here to help carry
situations.because: they have been taking the cave out a sack at a time
situations.offer: carry a sack and they will show you every way out they use

situations.doing: standing at the mouth with a gap in the row
situations.onArrival: the objects on it are dusted and the gap is not
situations.because: everybody leaves something and somebody took theirs back
situations.offer: fill the gap and the cave lets you out again afterwards

situations.doing: standing in a chamber with a shape clearly inside it
situations.onArrival: the shape is facing the way you came in
situations.because: the cave keeps things and this is how
situations.offer: speak to it and it answers, and it knows what the cave wants

situations.doing: lying dug through in one place with the spoil beside it
situations.onArrival: the newest bones are on top and one of them is clean
situations.because: the dead are left where they fall and grown over
situations.offer: put the clean bone back and the floor lets you cross anywhere

temptations.cue: the stone that let something go
temptations.benefit: once, get a thing out that the cave has kept
temptations.standingDrawback: the cave takes the nearest equivalent, and chooses

temptations.cue: something off the mouth shelf
temptations.benefit: once, be owed a way out
temptations.standingDrawback: you took somebody's passage out, and they are still in here

temptations.cue: a clean bone off the floor
temptations.benefit: once, be recognised by the Kept
temptations.standingDrawback: they recognise you as one of them

temptations.cue: a piece of broken formation
temptations.benefit: once, have exactly the thing the cave grew over
temptations.standingDrawback: the cave grows over you a little each time you rest

temptations.cue: a cast of the stone hand
temptations.benefit: once, be greeted rather than swallowed
temptations.standingDrawback: the greeting is binding both ways
